name: fix_ruby_hash_shared_default_array
description: Fixes a grouping method that uses Hash.new([]) with <<, so all keys share one default array and none are stored
prompts: Grouper#group in lib/grouper.rb should group the given words into a Hash keyed by each word's first letter, mapping to an array of the words that start with that letter (in input order). It's broken: it builds the hash with Hash.new([]) and appends with <<, so every << mutates the one shared default array and no keys are ever actually stored - group(['apple','ant','bee'])['a'] comes back with every word, and a missing key returns that same shared array. Fix group so each distinct first letter maps to its own array containing exactly its words, and looking up a letter that never appeared returns an empty array. Keep the class name and the group(words) signature.

setup_files.lib/grouper.rb:
module App
  class Grouper
    # Group words by their first letter.
    # BUG: Hash.new([]) hands out ONE shared default array and `<<` mutates
    # it in place without ever assigning the key, so the result hash stays
    # empty while the shared array collects everything.
    def group(words)
      result = Hash.new([])
      words.each { |w| result[w[0]] << w }
      result
    end
  end
end

test_setup_files.test/grouper_test.rb:
require "minitest/autorun"
require_relative "../lib/grouper"

class GrouperTest < Minitest::Test
  def setup
    @grouper = App::Grouper.new
  end

  def test_groups_by_first_letter
    result = @grouper.group(["apple", "ant", "bee"])
    assert_equal ["apple", "ant"], result["a"]
    assert_equal ["bee"], result["b"]
  end

  def test_missing_key_returns_empty_array
    result = @grouper.group(["apple"])
    assert_equal [], result["z"]
  end

  def test_preserves_input_order
    result = @grouper.group(["bat", "ball", "bee"])
    assert_equal ["bat", "ball", "bee"], result["b"]
  end

  def test_empty_input
    assert_equal [], @grouper.group([])["a"]
  end
end

reference_solution.lib/grouper.rb:
module App
  class Grouper
    # Group words by their first letter. The default block assigns a fresh
    # array per key on first access, so keys are stored and never shared.
    def group(words)
      result = Hash.new { |hash, key| hash[key] = [] }
      words.each { |w| result[w[0]] << w }
      result
    end
  end
end
